claims.text: Controlled thermal annealing or mechanical treatment can introduce moderate lattice strain into nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs without causing phase segregation.
Induced lattice strain alters the d-band center of surface atoms in PtPdRhRuIrOs.
Lattice strain modifies the adsorption energies of ethanol and its reaction intermediates.
The strain-induced electronic-structure change enhances adsorption of ethanol and reactive intermediates.
Electronic properties of multielement alloy active sites can modulate reactant chemisorption and catalytic performance.
Enhanced binding of reactive intermediates improves electron-transfer kinetics during ethanol oxidation.
Improved electron-transfer kinetics increase the catalytic oxidation rate of ethanol.
Moderately strained PtPdRhRuIrOs will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the pristine unstrained catalyst.
Moderately strained PtPdRhRuIrOs will exhibit a lower ethanol-oxidation overpotential than the pristine unstrained catalyst.
The appropriate baseline is a pristine PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticle catalyst with uniform elemental distribution and an unstrained lattice, tested under identical reaction conditions.
The proposed effect is expected under alkaline electrochemical ethanol-oxidation conditions at ambient temperature while catalyst stability is maintained.
The predicted behavior applies only while strain remains moderate enough to preserve solid-solution integrity.
Excessive strain may cause phase segregation or other significant structural changes that invalidate the predicted behavior.
A measurable d-band-center shift and improved ethanol-oxidation activity should occur together in the strained catalyst.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes phase-segregated catalysts from the hypothesis, whereas the falsification rule treats phase segregation caused by the intervention as falsifying the mechanism. Segregation would instead indicate failure to realize the stipulated moderate-strain intervention or operation outside the stated boundary.
